text:
sofia: quick follow-up from yesterday's kernel-path RFC — ran a short staging canary mixing L4 and H100 nodes. saw an sm capability mismatch: L4 reported no fp16/tensor cores, fell back to generic attn kernel, p99 increased ~18ms.

alex: do you have the logs/traces from the request that hit the fallback?

sofia: pasted a tiny snippet below, full logs in staging cluster 7.
```
[2026-03-18T22:13:04Z] node=l4-07 sm_caps=0x04 arch="l4" chosen_kernel="attn_generic" fallback_reason="no_fp16"
[2026-03-18T22:13:04Z] dispatch_time_ms=3 exec_time_ms=21 total_latency_ms=39
```

marta: thanks. this matches a pattern I saw earlier — L4's driver reports reduced SM feature flags for some firmware levels. suggestion: canonicalize probe to use both sm_cap bitmask + vendor microarch string (e.g., "l4_1.2.0") and cache at node agent level.

kevin: per-SM probing is expensive if we do it full-scan. tradeoff: sample first 16 requests to a node and run a lightweight microkernel probe (fast kernel that checks fp16/int8 paths) then flip a boolean in node-local cache. refresh on driver/firmware change.

priya: plus add a stale TTL (24h) and an on-startup probe. that reduces noise for bursty autoscaled nodes.

sofia: agree. also noticed KV cache reuse interacts with kernel path selection when sequence lengths vary — if we probe with short sequences we might pick a kernel suboptimal for long context. propose probing across the two most common seq lengths we see per route (e.g., 64 and 2048).

alex: sounds reasonable. want to avoid 2x probe cost on startup though. maybe staggered: probe short first, then background probe for long.

marta: implementation sketch (node-agent):
```yaml
probe_policy:
  init_sample: 16
  seq_lengths: [64, 2048]
  ttl_seconds: 86400
  refresh_on_driver_change: true
```

kevin: important metric hooks: fallback_count, probe_failures, kernel_selection_latency, dispatch_mismatch_rate. add a histogram for delta between chosen vs best-known kernel (measured via microbench).

priya: test plan: 1) canary 10% nodes with new probe+cache; 2) watch fallback_count and p99 for routes 3) run adversarial trace (long sequences + mixed batch) and compare cost/token.

sofia: put up a small PR with node-agent probe + config and a runtime flag `--sm-probe=enabled` so we can toggle during rollout: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1423

alex: example gating rule for runtime (pseudo):
```json
{"gates": [{"name": "fp16_core","required_bits": "0x08","kernel_hint": "attn_fp16"},{"name":"int8_accel","required_bits":"0x20","kernel_hint":"attn_int8"}], "default_kernel":"attn_generic"}
```

marta: small gotcha: some kernels are numerically different (int8 quant rounding). add a quality-check on rollout: compare logits/sequences on a sample prompt set and alert if regression > epsilon.

kevin: rollout schedule proposal: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%, with automated rollback if fallback_count increases by >200% or p99 increases by >10ms for 30m window.

infra-bot: canary job scheduled: job_id=canary-sm-probe-1981234600, start=1981234605

sofia: I'll wire alerts and the eval harness. also will add a vendor-firmware map to known_quirks so we can short-circuit probes for devices with verified flags.

deploy-bot: deploy queued (canary-sm-probe-1981234600) — ETA ~4m

priya: one last note — for L4 specifically, ensure quantized graph builder prefers int8 kernels when available; fallback to fp16 only if numeric check passes.

sofia: thanks all — I'll update the RFC with the probe contract (how node agents report sm_caps, probe timestamps, and kernel_hint). putting follow-up items in the RFC thread and the PR. :thumbsup:
